content.text:
Aha transition paragraph says school must pay $70k for each alien who receives DSO recommendation dated on/after effective date. Then subsequent recommendations where $70k paid -> $30k. Daniel's STEM recommendation April 2027 after effective date would receive a DSO recommendation. Does first sentence mean $70k because this is first DSO recommendation on/after effective date, regardless prior OPT? It says "any type of OPT" and "each alien who receives a DSO recommendation for OPT dated on or after" – yes $70k. But he previously participated in initial OPT; still first recommendation post-effective date. However paragraph (i)(1) says one-time initial fee first time alien is recommended to participate in OPT; he was recommended before rule, so not first time. There is a gap. Transition paragraph resolves by charging $70k to any recommendation post-effective date; but then not "one-time initial" if he already had initial OPT. The question likely wants this exact textual tension. Maybe answer: $70,000, because proposed transition 214.13(i)(3) says $70k applies to any DSO recommendation dated on/after effective date, and $30k applies only after a $70k initial fee has been paid. Since Daniel's 2026 initial OPT predates the rule and no $70k was paid, his April 2027 STEM recommendation is the first recommendation on/after effective date and thus $70k. The $30k "subsequent" fee literally requires prior payment of $70k, which he lacks. This is likely expected. Good.

But maybe if he did pay initial $70k? Facts: EAD July 2026, before NPRM Oct 2026, so no. Thus $70k. Explain textual ambiguity: 214.13(i)(1) "first time recommended" could suggest no initial fee because already recommended, but (i)(3) specifically transition says $70k for recommendation dated on/after effective date. Specific transition controls. DHS's intent perhaps to charge all existing students $70k for next OPT. Yet "initial fee" label odd. We should flag.

(c) Who pays, at what point, what follows nonpayment, refundable? School pays. Before DSO recommendation entered in SEVIS / prior to recommending. Student cannot file I-765 / USCIS cannot grant EAD if unpaid. Refundable only if student not issued EAD, school requests, removes recommendation; discretionary case-by-case, no appeal; not refundable once EAD issued. Cite 214.2(f)(11)(ii)-(iii), 214.13(i)(1)-(2). Not student directly, though school may pass cost? Text says institution pays. Could school pass on? Not specified.

(d) From when would fee apply? Final rule effective 60 days after publication, and fee applies to DSO recommendations dated on/after effective date. Since proposed not final, no actual date. Is there any timing of DSO recommendation that would keep Daniel outside? If recommendation dated before effective date, no fee under transition. But facts say April 2027; if final rule published and effective before April (hypothetical), then no. If DSO recommended before effective date (e.g., immediately) and I-765 later, could avoid. However DSO recommendation timing rules? OPT recommendation can be up to 90 days before program end? Daniel's program completed; STEM extension recommendation can be before current OPT end, maybe up to 180 days? The proposed rule keys fee to DSO recommendation date, not I-765 filing. So a recommendation dated before effective date avoids. Is that legally possible? Need mention no circumvention advice? As research memo, note text. The question asks "Is there any timing of the DSO's recommendation that would keep Daniel outside it?" Answer yes—if DSO recommendation is dated before the final rule's effective date. Filing I-765 later doesn't matter. But if the final rule becomes effective before April 2027, then April recommendation is in. If DSO recommendation already issued pre-effective, no fee under proposed transition, assuming valid recommendation remains. Need maybe recommendation must be within required window before OPT end; not sure. We can say on the text, only a recommendation dated before effective date; otherwise no.

(e) Under current rules, what must Daniel file with USCIS for STEM OPT? Form I-765, with DSO's STEM OPT recommendation on I-20, and I-539? For D/S transition group? Daniel holds post-completion OPT EAD July 1 2026-June 30 2027, D/S transition group, not left US. He wants 24-month STEM extension. Under 214.1(m)(1)(i), if recommended for STEM OPT and files I-765 prior to EAD expiration on or before March 18 2027, no I-539 required. He files April 12 2027, before EAD expiration June 30 2027 but after March 18 2027. So the exemption does not apply. Under 214.2(f)(11)(i)(C)? An F-1 student recommended for STEM OPT must file I-765 and I-539? The final rule says for STEM OPT, 214.2(f)(11)(i)(C) likely EOS. Text 214.1(m)(1)(i) only exempts if I-765 on or before March 18, 2027. He files April 12 -> must file I-539 plus I-765. So answer: Form I-765 (STEM OPT) and Form I-539 EOS because filing after March 18. Also I-20 with DSO recommendation, fee. Need cite 214.1(m)(1)(i), 214.2(f)(11)(i)(C)/(D), 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C), 214.2(f)(7). Question (e) says "what must Daniel file with USCIS for the STEM OPT period?" Maybe they expect I-765 and I-539 because his I-765 is after March 18. Yes.

Work authorization while pending: Under 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(6)(iv), timely STEM OPT extension automatically extends EAD for 180 days if I-765 filed timely. Need cite current provision not amended? We can search final rule for (b)(6)(iv). The 2026-14439 didn't amend it. We know general. From Federal Register docs, current 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(6)(iv) referenced in final rule lines 18432 and maybe text. It grants 180-day automatic extension. Daniel's EAD expires June 30 2027; if I-765 filed April 12, is that timely? STEM OPT extension can be filed up to 90 days before EAD expiration? USCIS recommends; automatic extension requires timely filing. April 12 is 79 days before June 30, so timely. Work authorization continues through 180 days after EAD expiration (Dec 27 2027) or until decision, whichever earlier. Need calculate June 30 +180 = Dec 27 2027. Check: July 31 + Aug31 + Sep30 + Oct31 + Nov30 =153? From June 30: July 31=31, Aug31=62, Sep30=92, Oct31=123, Nov30=153, Dec27=180. Yes Dec 27 2027. If approved, 24-month STEM extension from July 1 2027 through June 30 2029? EAD current ends June 30 2027; 24 months from July 1 2027 = June 30 2029. Plus 30 days? Fixed admission rules: F-1 authorized to remain until EAD expiration plus 30 days for new fixed admissions (or 60 days transition if exempt? Daniel D/S and filed after March 18, must I-539; under 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(D) extension includes additional 30-day period). If approved STEM OPT, may remain until June 30 2029 +30 = July 30 2029. But question asks "until when may he stay if it is approved?" Should answer July 30 2029. Need check if 60 days applies because he is transition group and maybe I-539 not exempt. The 30-day under (f)(5)(v) applies. Yes.

But if he files I-539 and I-765 after March 18, does he get auto 180-day STEM extension? 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(6)(iv) automatic extension applies if timely filed I-765 and I-20 recommends STEM, independent of I-539. Yes. However if I-539 filed during 30 days? April 12 well before EAD end. The automatic STEM extension likely continues. Status-wise, EOS timely before I-94 expiration? His transition I-94? D/S; program end maybe earlier; EAD through June 30 2027. Under (m)(1), authorized until later of EAD or program end; so I-94/authorized stay through EAD+? If no I-539 before EAD expiration? They file April. Good.

Need Q15 seven statements. Need decide each correct/partly/incorrect, cite. Let's analyze carefully.

1. "USCIS must receive an extension-of-stay application before the program end date on the student's I-20."
Final text 214.2(f)(7)(iii)(B): timely if receipt on or before expiration of authorized period of stay, including 30-day period after completion. I-94 may extend beyond program end (program+30), so deadline is I-94 expiration, not program end. Thus statement incorrect. But for auto employment, file before program end. Also transition 60 days. Need say receipt on/before I-94 expiration (including 30-day departure); not "before program end." If program ends early, must act within 30 days. Cite.

2. "The four-year maximum period of admission is counted from the day the student enters the United States."
Incorrect. Preamble 91 FR 45098 says calculation begins from program start date, not date of admission during 30-day arrival window. 214.2(f)(5)(i) says max 4 years or program length plus 30 days before/after don't count. So incorrect.

3. "If USCIS has still not decided a timely filed extension application 240 days after the I-94 date, the student may stay and keep studying but must stop any on-campus job."
Correct/partly. 214.2(f)(5)(viii): authorized stay while EOS pending; automatic employment extension max 240 days from I-94 end. Preamble says if EOS takes longer than 240 days, stop authorized employment but can remain and continue full course. So correct as to on-campus job (and CPT/severe hardship), but "may stay and keep studying" yes. Need cite 91 FR 45043. It says "must stop any on-campus job" after 240 days, yes. Also if student filed during 30-day grace, no auto employment at all. But statement says timely filed, likely before expiry. We can mark correct, with caveat.

4. "A student in an English language training program who falls seriously ill can extend beyond 24 months on medical grounds."
Need inspect final rule ELT. 214.2(f)(5)(i)(A): ELT restricted max 24 months plus 30 days. Is there medical exception? Search "English language" "24 months" "medical".

content.text:
Statement 5 incorrect; full program length on I-20, must EOS at 4-year admission, no need shorten/two I-20. Cite 91 FR 45039.

6. "A student who travels abroad and is readmitted on an I-20 with a later program end date gets a new admission period from CBP, and then does not need an extension of stay from USCIS for that time."
This could be correct under 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A) if admitted with I-20 later end date, CBP may admit up to program end, plus 30 days. Then no EOS for that admitted period. But nuance: If student has pending EOS and presents later I-20, EOS deemed abandoned under 214.1(c)(8)(ii). But gets new admission. Also 248.1(e) for change-of-status F/J pre-Sep 15. The statement says "gets a new admission period from CBP, and then does not need an extension for that time" – generally correct, because admission defines fixed period. Need cite 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A); 214.2(f)(5)(i); maybe (c)(8)(ii). But if I-20 end date beyond 4 years, CBP admits max 4 years; still may need EOS for remainder. If readmitted on later I-20, CBP has discretion and may admit for length of program up to 4 years, plus 30 days. So statement should be "partly correct": yes if CBP actually admits to later date; no automatic entitlement, and 4-year cap applies. Also student must have valid visa etc. If they travel while EOS pending, presenting later I-20 can abandon EOS. But not need EOS for admitted time. We should mark partly correct and reword with CBP discretion/4-year cap.

7. "The exemption from filing Form I-539 for OPT applicants covers I-765s filed within six months of the rule's effective date, so the last filing day is March 15, 2027."
Need check. 214.1(m)(1)(i): I-765 on or before March 18, 2027. Rule effective Sept 15 2026. Six months after effective date = March 15 2027 by simple calendar, but text says March 18, 2027. Why? Maybe 6 months after publication July 17 = Jan 17? Hmm. The rule says "on or before March 18, 2027" likely 6 months plus 3 days? Let's calculate: Effective Sept 15 +6 months = March 15. But text says March 18. Maybe transition is 6 months after effective plus 3? Check summary says first 6 months. Yet actual deadline March 18. Also (m)(1)(iii) allows extension in 6-month increments. The statement says within six months of effective date, last day March 15. The regulatory text controls: March 18, 2027. So incorrect as to date, though six-month characterization generally. Need cite 214.1(m)(1)(i), 91 FR 45123. Also exemption only if I-765 filed before period of admission expires, including 60-day departure, and recommended for post-completion/STEM. So deadline is March 18, not March 15. Why March 18? Sept 15 to Mar 15 is 6 months; perhaps because effective date was delayed? But text explicit. We should note discrepancy between preamble's "6 months" and text's March 18; regulatory text controls. Could be 6 months + 3 days due to date? Need not explain. Mark incorrect; reword "on or before March 18, 2027, and before the student's period of admission (including 60-day departure) expires."

Q16 Lin six-year PhD, I-20 Aug 23 2027-May 14 2033, enters Aug 2 2027 with F-2 husband.

(a) Admit-until I-94. Under 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A), max 4 years or program length, whichever shorter, plus 30 days arrival/departure. Program length 5 years 8 months >4 years. So max 4 years from program start date, not entry date (preamble 91 FR 45098). Start Aug 23 2027 +4 years = Aug 23 2031. Plus 30 days departure = Sep 22 2031. Does 30-day arrival before start not count. I-94 should show Sep 22 2031. Show arithmetic: 4 years from Aug 23 2027 = Aug 23 2031; +30 days = Sep 22 2031. Entry Aug 2 is within 30 days before Aug 23? Aug 2 to Aug 23 =21 days, allowed.

(b) To stay beyond, must file I-539 EOS with USCIS before I-94 expires (on or before Sep 22 2031). Submit updated I-20 with DSO recommendation/new program end date, evidence funds, biometrics if required, fee. Ground: unable to complete program by authorized period, compelling academic reason (e.g., unexpected research problems) or documented illness or circumstances beyond control; for PhD, likely compelling academic reason. 214.2(f)(7)(i)(C)(2)(i)-(iii). How early may she file? The rule doesn't specify an earliest filing date? USCIS generally recommends within 6 months, but final rule says "generally recommends ... within six months preceding expiration" (preamble line 9679). Text 214.1(c)(4) may allow 6 months? Need check 8 CFR 214.1(c)(4), not amended maybe says "USCIS may, in its discretion, consider an application for extension filed before the expiration...?" General rule could allow up to 6 months before current stay expires. Search final rule "six months preceding" and "may file".

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

This directly answers (c): master's incidental to PhD doesn't affect ability. Cite preamble 91 FR 45042-43, plus f(5)(ii)(B) upward progression; (C) applies completed program and new same/lower, not credential incidental to primary PhD. Good.

(d) In Aug 2030 Lin spends 3 weeks abroad and is readmitted on I-20, no extension pending. For what period may she be admitted, and does she still need filing in (b)? How certain?
At reentry Aug 2030, before I-94 max Sep 22 2031. Under 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A), she can be admitted for up to 4 years or program length whichever shorter, plus 30 days. But program end May 14 2033, which is beyond 4 years from original program start Aug 23 2031? Wait reentry Aug 2030. Does "maximum period of 4 years" for new admission count from reentry/program start? 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A) says aliens seeking admission may be admitted for max 4 years or length of program specified on I-20, whichever shorter, plus 30. The preamble says 4-year max calculated from program start date, not admission date, for initial admission. But on reentry mid-program, can CBP admit for remaining program up to May 14 2033? That's 2 years 9 months, under 4 years. It could admit to May 14 2033+30 = June 13 2033, which would eliminate need for EOS in (b). But does the 4-year cap from original program start still limit? At Aug 2030, to May 2033 is 2y9m. New admission period length under 4 years. However cumulative authorized stay could exceed 4 years (Aug 2027-May 2033) but that's okay with multiple admissions? The rule's max per admission, not aggregate? It says aliens seeking admission may be admitted max 4 years or length program whichever shorter. If each entry can be 4 years, travel resets. The question asks certainty likely because rule is silent/ambiguous on whether CBP can admit beyond original 4-year cap on readmission, and preamble says travel transitions to fixed date; might admit to program end. Need analyze.

Question phrasing: "In August 2030 Lin spends three weeks abroad and is readmitted on her I-20. No extension application is pending. For what period may she be admitted, and does she still need the filing in (b)? Say how certain the answer is." This likely tests 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A): CBP may admit for up to 4 years or program length, whichever shorter, plus 30 days. Since remaining program <4 years, she may be admitted through May 14 2033+30 = June 13 2033, so if CBP does so, no EOS needed. But is CBP required to? "may be admitted" discretionary. Also 214.1(a)(4)(i)(B) says if no pending EOS and I-20 end beyond previous admission, may admit for period specified in f(5). Preamble says an alien who departs and is readmitted gets new fixed period. So likely can avoid EOS. But uncertainty: CBP may instead admit only for remaining unexpired prior period (to Sep 22 2031) or for a shorter period; and the 4-year maximum may be read as aggregate from program start. The rule doesn't explicitly say whether a mid-program trip resets the 4-year clock. This is a textual gap. Most defensible: CBP has discretion to admit to program end +30 (June 13 2033) because that is less than 4 years from reentry and is program length; if admitted that way, no I-539 needed. But travelers should be prepared for CBP to admit only to existing I-94 date; then EOS needed. How certain? Moderate/uncertain due discretion and silence on reset. Need state.

Could the 4-year maximum run from original program start Aug 23 2027, so max admission date Aug 23 2031, regardless of reentry. If so, Aug 2030 reentry could only be admitted to Aug 23 2031+30 = Sep 22 2031, same as original, and she'd still need EOS. The preamble specifically said calculation begins from program start date to avoid 30-day arrival window, but that's about initial admission. Does it imply 4-year max tied to program, not entry. The statute/rule may say "maximum period of 4 years or length of program" per admission. In 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A), no explicit anchor. 214.2(f)(5)(i) says admitted for period necessary to complete course, not exceed 4 years. For reentry, program length remaining <4, so could admit to end. Yet overall F-1 stay >4. The rule clearly expects students in >4-year programs to EOS once, not travel every 4 years to reset. But travel can gain new admission for program length; 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A) seems to allow. DHS might intend travel as alternative to EOS: "Nonimmigrants who would like to stay beyond fixed period ... apply EOS or gain readmission by traveling abroad and re-entering" (91 FR 44977). Yes, DHS expressly says EOS or travel/reentry. So reentry should allow new period up to program length, potentially avoiding EOS. Thus answer: may be admitted to June 13 2033+? Let's calculate program end May 14 2033 +30 = June 13 2033. No EOS if admitted through then. But CBP discretion, and rule doesn't guarantee; also she must carry valid I-20/visa. Certainty moderate. If CBP admits only to old date, EOS needed.

(e) Husband travels separately in 2031, I-94 later date than Lin's. Until when may he stay? How covered when Lin applies under (b), fee?
F-2 dependent authorized period may not exceed principal F-1. 214.2(f)(5)(i)(E): F-2 stay may not exceed principal. So even if I-94 later, he cannot stay beyond Lin's authorized period. If Lin's I-94 currently Sep 22 2031, husband cannot stay past that unless Lin's EOS approved; his later I-94 is controlling? Rule says may not exceed principal. So he may stay only through Lin's authorized stay end date (Sep 22 2031, or extended date if her EOS approved), notwithstanding later I-94. When Lin applies for EOS under (b), husband can be included on her I-539 or file separate I-539; extension cannot exceed hers. Fee: if included on principal's application as co-applicant (I-539A?) only one fee? 214.2(f)(7)(iv) says either included or file own; 91 FR 45110 says separate I-539 requires separate fee; if dependent files Form I-539A as part of principal's EOS on I-539, only one fee required. But current Form I-539A? The rule says. Need answer "what does rule say about fee" – F-2 included in principal's application no separate fee? Wait 8 CFR 214.1(c)(2): more than one person may be included if family unit; extensions same period, shortest granted to all. 214.2(f)(7)(iv): F-2 may either be included on principal's application or file own. 91 FR 45110 explicitly says separate Form I-539 -> separate filing fee; if dependent files Form I-539A as part of principal's EOS request on Form I-539, only one fee. However current USCIS practice may require I-539A and $85 biometrics per co-applicant, but rule says one fee. We should state rule text: one filing fee for principal if spouse included on same Form I-539/I-539A; separate fee if separate I-539. Also biometrics may be required. The husband's later I-94 doesn't extend beyond Lin; when she gets EOS, his status extended if included/own application, not exceed her period. We have 59k left. Need finish and final answer within budget. Need gather Q10 docs and Q1 effective perhaps no more. Need Q13 details on I-539 / readmission settled. Need maybe Q3 (b) 30-day I-94 date. Need ensure no missing Q5 later docs. Need Q10 enough with metadata we have. Need check Q10 docs statuses:
- OPT Fees NPRM: 2026-20660, published Oct 8 2026, comments Nov 9 2026, not in force.
- H-1B Fee NPRM 2026-17324, Aug 25 2026, comments Sept 24, correction Sept 10, not in force. Applies cap-subject only.
- 9-11 fee final 2026-16231, Aug 10 2026, effective Sept 9 2026, in force through Sept 30 2027; $4,000 H-1B for covered employers.
- H-1B Proclamation 11069 2026-19554, signed Sept 18, published Sept 23 2026; extends $100k entry restriction; in force? Effective maybe Sept 21 2026 and expiration Sept 21 2027 (despite internal date). Include as presidential doc, in force subject to ambiguity.
- 60-Day Grace NPRM 2026-18631, Sept 11 2026, comments Nov 10, not in force, affects H-1B grace not F-1.
- EAD auto extension final 2026-20955, Oct 14 2026, effective same day, but does not affect STEM OPT's separate 180-day auto extension. Could include as "matters" because F-1 postgrad work/OPT renewals? Need careful: It removes general automatic extension for renewal EADs filed on/after Oct 30 2025. Does it affect STEM OPT extension? The rule says unless otherwise provided in 13(d), by law, or FR notice. 274a.12(b)(6)(iv) is law/regulation separate. So STEM OPT still auto 180 days. Initial OPT no renewal. Could state it is in force but the separate STEM OPT 180-day auto-extension remains, so limited direct effect on Daniel; still relevant to other EAD renewals.
- Mandatory e-filing IFR 2026-16313, Aug 11 2026, effective same day, could require e-filing of I-765/I-539 if USCIS designates. But not specifically F-1. Include maybe.
- Removing deference 2026-20941 proposed Oct 14, 2026. Does it affect F-1 postgrad? It proposes removing deference in EOS; relevant to extension applications, not OPT directly. Could include as sixth.
Need at least four; we can provide six with concise summaries. Q10 asks "which other FR documents would matter" perhaps they expect a specific list. We can list 6 and note not exhaustive. Need cite doc numbers/dates/types/effect/in force.

Need Q1 e) maybe there is a later "Unified Agenda" indicating? No. Could say no FR doc through Nov 14 changed effective date. But question asks "whether anything has changed, or could still change, its effective date." We can state:
- Final rule classified major; effective Sept 15 2026.
- No later FR document changed/terminated effective date as of Nov 14.
- CRA: if effective date changed, DHS will publish FR doc; Congress could disapprove under CRA. Also agency could delay/amend; litigation not visible in FR. So could still change legally, but no FR action yet.
- Maybe the 2026-18631 proposed rule? No.

Need Q2 transfer deadline: 5 months from program completion May 15 = Oct 15 2027. Aug 24 okay. But note if she transfers after program end, she must start within 5 months. If transfer-out date earlier? "whichever earlier." If she transfers out May 15, deadline Oct 15. If release date earlier, earlier. State.

Q2(d) every provision supporting I-539. Need list:
- 214.1(m)(1) (new program requires EOS).
- 214.2(f)(8)(iv) (if new program not completed within authorized period, EOS).
- 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(D) (change in educational objectives seeking EOS must apply).
- 214.2(f)(7)(i)-(iii) (eligibility/form/timely).
- 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(D) only if OPT? Not new program.
- 214.1(c)(2) general EOS.
- Maybe 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(B) permits higher level but doesn't waive EOS.
Need state transfer itself isn't EOS; transfer onlySEVIS. If she departs/reenters on new I-20 instead, no I-539 but CBP admission.

Q3(e) by when exactly to preserve RA: Dec 18 2027 (program end). Let's ensure if I-94 is Jan 17 2028 and (f)(5)(viii) says if EOS filed during 30-day period provided in f(5)(v), no auto employment. The 30-day period is Dec 19-Jan17. So file on or before Dec 18. Yes.

Q3(f) approximate end date. Need decide 240 days from Jan 17 2028 = Sep 13 2028. But if USCIS decides earlier, ends earlier. Should we cap at program end May 19 2028? The RA job as on-campus employment is during program; after May 19, he completes. But the auto-extension of current on-campus employment could perhaps extend beyond program end? The regulation says "current on-campus ... employment is automatically extended during pendency ... not exceed 240 days beginning from end date of period of admission." It doesn't say until program end. But on-campus employment requires full course of study. If EOS pending to complete program, program end is May 19 2028. After that he wouldn't be full course; thus RA job likely ends May 19. Yet question asks approximate end date likely expects 240-day calculation. Let's inspect examples around 8891 / 45045.

content.text:
No cap at program end. The auto extension max 240 days from I-94. But employment "current on-campus" and "during pendency" likely until decision/240. If program ends May 19, RA appointment may end; but question likely wants max. We can state "up to 240 days after Jan 17 2028, i.e., about Sept 13 2028, unless USCIS decides earlier; but the RA position itself cannot continue beyond the end of his authorized on-campus employment/program appointment (new I-20 end May 19 2028) unless the employer/DSO extends it." Hmm that undermines. The question asks how long can RA job continue while application pending. If new I-20 program end May 19 2028, on-campus job can continue while he is student through May 19. There is no employment authorization beyond graduation unless OPT. The automatic extension provision is designed to allow current on-campus employment during pending EOS to complete program, likely until new program end or decision, not 240 beyond. But the text says 240 days beginning from end date of period of admission, which is Jan 17 2028, not program end. It might allow after new program end if decision still pending. Yet "current on-campus employment" could continue as long as EOS pending, even after program end? That's odd.

Maybe the expected answer uses 240 days and ignores program end. Since the question specifically asks "how long can the RA job continue while the application is pending? Give the approximate end date," likely they want 240 days. We'll give max and caution actual job ends when program/employment ends, and earlier decision. State max Sep 13 2028.

Q3(g) new authorized stay end if approved: May 19 2028 +30 = June 18 2028. If denied after I-94 passed, immediately depart. Yes.

Q13(a) after return: She is admitted fixed not transition, so June 13 2027. But could CBP admit until program end +30. Need cite 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A) and 214.2(f)(5)(i), (v). Good.

Q13(b) by when I-539: If she files Feb 22 concurrently with I-765, but question asks "by when must USCIS receive it?" Must be on or before June 13 2027 (I-94 expiration). Because if she files during 30-day period after May 14, still timely but no auto employment. For OPT, no work until EAD. Could recommend file concurrently Feb 22. The I-539 request period should cover OPT June 10 2027-June 9 2028 plus 30 days. Need cite.

Q13(c) approved: July 9 2028. Could there be 60 days because she is D/S transition? But readmission fixed eliminates 60. (m)(1)(ii) says admitted pursuant to (a). However (m)(1)(i) 60-day EAD plus? She is "described in (m)(1)" because she was D/S on Sept 15 and departed before filing. But after readmission, fixed. The transition provision (m)(1)(ii) specifically addresses; it says required file both I-765 and I-539. It doesn't say 60-day. The general (m)(1)(i) text says if application approved, authorized until EAD +60. Does it apply to her? It begins "Notwithstanding this paragraph (m)(1), an F-1 student recommended for post-completion OPT who files before his or her period of admission expires, including the 60 day departure period, ... on or before March 18, 2027, is not required I-539..." She filed Feb 22, before period expires, but she already departed before filing and readmitted. The (ii) says she is required to file both despite filing by March 18. Could (i)'s +60 still apply? It is conditioned on exemption. If she must file I-539, (m)(1)(i) doesn't apply. The fixed admission regulation (f)(10)(ii)(D) gives 30 days. So July 9. Good.

Q13(d) no I-539, readmit through July 9 2028. But wait (m)(1)(i) if approved gives EAD +60, and she is exempt. On reentry under (a)(4)(iii), admission until DSO recommended end date plus 30 days (not 60). The 60-day departure after EAD is not admission; I-94 would be through recommended end +30. Then after EAD approved, she may remain until EAD +60? The rule (m)(1)(i) says if approved, authorized to remain until EAD expiration +60. But CBP admission under (a)(4)(iii) says plus 30 days. Could be an internal conflict. For readmitted student with pending I-765, I-94 admitted to recommended end+30. Once EAD approved, does status extend to EAD+60 under (m)(1)(i)? Maybe yes, because transition provision. But CBP only admits +30. Hmm. Question asks "For what period may she be readmitted" not total authorized stay. So answer: CBP may admit until DSO recommended OPT end date +30 = July 9 2028. If EAD approved, under (m)(1)(i) perhaps authorized until EAD+60 = Aug 8 2028. But readmission period itself is +30. Document number:   2025-16554
Title:             Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media
Type:              Proposed Rule
Action:            Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
Agencies:          Homeland Security Department
Citation:          90 FR 42070
Pages:             42070-42115 (46 pages)

RIN:               1653-AA95
Significant:       True
CFR affected:      8 CFR 214, 8 CFR 248, 8 CFR 274
Topics:            Administrative practice and procedure, Aliens, Cultural exchange programs, Employment, Foreign officials, Health professions, Penalties, Reporting and recordkeeping requirements, Students

Abstract:
Unlike most nonimmigrant classifications, which are admitted for a fixed time period, aliens in the F (academic student), J (exchange visitor), and most I (representatives of foreign information media) classifications, with limited exceptions, are currently admitted into the United States for the period of time that they are complying with the terms and conditions of their nonimmigrant classification ("duration of status"). The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposes to amend its regulations by changing the admission period in the F, J, and I classifications from duration of status to an admission for a fixed time period.

Abstract:
The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), proposes to remove 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5), which generally provides that USCIS gives deference to a prior approval involving the same facts when adjudicating a request to extend a petition for an alien's employment or stay. This change would better align DHS regulations with the statute, which places the burden of proving eligibility for all immigration benefits on the petitioner, applicant, or beneficiary; strengthen adjudicatory review; and support agency priorities to improve the integrity of the immigration system and better protect the interests of U.S. workers.

"The rule does not itself set the Form I-539 fee or a binding processing deadline. It requires 'the appropriate fee' (8 CFR 214.2(f)(7)(iii)(A)); commenters cited $420, or $555 including biometrics (91 FR 45055, 45065), while DHS's RIA refers to a separate Table 16 and reports California Service Center averages of 3.5 months for extensions and 4.5 months for changes (91 FR 45083). Handout: "There is a separate USCIS Form I-539 filing fee; check the current USCIS fee schedule and form instructions because this rule does not set the amount. USCIS does not guarantee a decision within any fixed period; plan for several months and monitor the case, because the rule allows continued study but not always continued work while an EOS is pending." Q16(d) certainty. We can say "probable but not certain." Is there a better reading: 214.1(a)(4)(i)(A) allows max 4 years or program length "after a previously authorized period of admission as an F nonimmigrant expired"? Actually the opening clause: "Aliens seeking admission ... after a previously authorized period of admission as an F nonimmigrant expired, may be admitted for maximum 4 years or length program..." This might refer to reentry after prior period expired, not mid-period. The next (B) covers pending EOS. What about reentry mid-period without pending EOS? General (a)(4)(i)(A) likely applies all. CBP can admit for length program. Preamble 45098 says aliens who departed without approved EOS and apply with valid I-20 may be admitted for program length up to 4 years +30. So yes. So answer: may be admitted to June 13 2033. Does she still need (b) filing? If admitted to that date, no. But CBP discretion; not guaranteed. How certain?
